rounds.text: Galaxy Surfactants is demonstrating a powerful operational turnaround that is not yet fully reflected in the valuation. The company reported its highest ever quarterly EBITDA of INR 252.5 crores, representing an 87% year-on-year surge alongside a dramatic expansion in EBITDA per metric ton to INR 35,458 [E84, E86]. This stellar profit acceleration is backed by exceptional top-line momentum, with trailing twelve-month sales growth hitting 27% [E17] and quarterly operating margins expanding by 4 percentage points year-on-year [E30]. The financial foundation supporting this growth is exceptionally robust, anchored by a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.09x and strong operational cash generation of INR 333 crores that fully covers reported profit with a 1.25x cash conversion rate [E33, E34, E36]. Furthermore, capital expenditure headwinds are subsiding as evidenced by a 30.9% drop in capital-work-in-progress, clearing the path for upcoming capacity additions like the Mexico EPC project scheduled for commercialization over the next twelve months [E39, E81]. Conceded: the near-term DCF valuation model flags overvaluation and institutional money flow shows a slight negative adjustment [E43, E66]. However, the core business fundamentals significantly outpace historical share price trends while operating within a favorable chemical sector tailwind [E55, E71].

The current market price of ₹2,175 reflects a significant valuation risk, as a discounted cash flow analysis suggests an intrinsic value of only ₹1,106, leaving a negative margin of safety of -96.7% [E2, E44, E45]. This pricing implies a 9.4% earnings growth rate according to a reverse DCF, which contrasts sharply with the company’s actual compounded profit growth of -2% over five years and -10% over three years [E19, E20, E46]. Operational vulnerabilities are evident in the AMET region, where volumes declined 15% year-on-year in Q4, and Egypt operations continue to face disruptions from geopolitical developments in West Asia [E88, E90]. Furthermore, management must contend with persistent headwinds including longer transit times, port congestion, and elevated freight costs [E91]. Conceded: the company is almost debt-free and recently achieved a record quarterly EBITDA of ₹252.5 crores [E58, E84]. Despite these recent gains, institutional money flow is negative, and the company’s return on equity of 10.9% remains well below its 10-year median of 18% [E13, E25, E43].

While the bear highlights a negative margin of safety based on a DCF [E44, E45], this model assumes 0% growth [E46], which is contradicted by the recent 110% year-on-year net profit surge and 27% trailing twelve-month sales growth [E17, E64, E70]. Conceded: historical 3-year and 5-year profit growth has been negative [E19, E20], yet the company is now "fundamentals-led" with profit growth outpacing price growth by 24% over the last year [E56]. Although AMET faced volume declines [E88, E90], the primary India engine grew by 11% [E79], and the Mexico EPC project remains on track for commercialization within 12 months [E81, E93]. Management has effectively navigated supply chain headwinds [E91] to deliver a record quarterly EBITDA of ₹252.5 crores [E84], subsequently raising full-year EBITDA per metric ton guidance to a range of ₹24,000 to ₹25,000 [E75]. Despite current ROE sitting below historical medians [E13, E25], quarterly operating margins have already expanded by 4 percentage points year-on-year to 14% [E30]. Finally, while institutional money flow is flagged as negative [E43], both foreign and domestic institutions have actually increased their percentage holdings since December 2023 [E41, E42].

Conceded: the company reported a record quarterly EBITDA of ₹252.5 crores and raised its full-year EBITDA per metric ton guidance to ₹24,000 to ₹25,000 [E75, E84], but this short-term operational spike does not erase the longer-term structural concerns flagged by a negative margin of safety under the DCF model [E44, E45]. While the bull dismisses the DCF’s zero-growth base assumption [E46], it ignores the reality that compounded profit growth over the past 3 years sits at -10% and over 5 years at -2% [E19, E20], demonstrating that past top-line improvements like the 27% TTM sales growth [E17] have persistently failed to convert into sustained bottom-line expansion. Furthermore, the bull points to institutional ownership changes [E41, E42] while downplaying the explicit negative money flow signal indicating ongoing institutional outflow [E43, E67]. Although the India engine and Mexico EPC project progress [E79, E81], operations in AMET continue to face disruptions from West Asian developments, port congestion, and elevated freight costs that require close monitoring [E90, E91]. Finally, the current ROE of 10.9% [E13] and low 3-year median ROE of 13% [E27] show that the underlying capital efficiency remains depressed well below its historical 10-year median of 18% [E25].

Conceded: 3-year profit growth sits at -10% and 5-year profit growth at -2% [E19, E20], reflecting past earnings headwinds. However, the bear relies on a static DCF model yielding -96.7% safety [E44, E45] while ignoring the company's powerful, accelerating reality: TTM sales jumped 27% [E17], quarterly net profit surged 110% YoY [E64], and quarterly operating margin expanded by 4 percentage points [E30] to hit a record quarterly EBITDA of ₹252.5 crores [E84]. While the bear cites negative institutional money flow [E43, E67], foreign and domestic institutional holders have actually increased their stakes since December 2023 [E41, E42]. The bear's focus on AMET disruptions [E90] overlooks strong volume growth elsewhere, such as India's 11% surge and the Americas' recovery [E79, E80], alongside the Mexico EPC project remaining firmly on track for commercialization within 12 months [E81]. Finally, although recent ROE sits at 10.9% [E13], the company operates with a conservatively financed debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.09x [E36], full cash conversion of 1.25x backing up its profits [E33], and a raised EBITDA per metric ton guidance of ₹24,000 to ₹25,000 [E75] that proves operational momentum is compounding.

Conceded: TTM sales jumped 27% [E17] and quarterly net profit surged 110% YoY [E64]. However, the bull's dismissal of the DCF model's -96.7% safety margin [E44, E45] ignores the underlying fundamental reality that 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growth remain negative at -2% and -10% respectively [E19, E20], dragging long-term share price growth down by -8% and -6% over the same periods [E22, E23]. While the bull highlights increasing institutional stakes since December 2023 [E41, E42], the scanX signal engine explicitly flags the current institutional money flow as negative with a holding change of -0.27 percentage points [E43]. The bull points to India's 11% volume surge and Americas' recovery [E79, E80] to downplay AMET disruptions, yet management itself explicitly warns that West Asia developments created significant disruptions in April and early May, with Egypt operations affected and elevated freight costs requiring close monitoring [E90, E91, E92]. Furthermore, while the debt-to-equity ratio is low at 0.09x [E36], borrowings actually increased to Rs 235 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 210 Cr a year prior [E38], and the company's recent ROE of 10.9% [E13] and 3-year low ROE of 12.9% [E60] confirm that rich valuation multiples of 21.2x P/E and 2.81x P/B [E1, E2] are not currently backed by elite capital efficiency.

evidence.quote: As regards to our guidance for the full year, we maintain our volume guidance at 6% to 8% for the full-year FY26-27, but I, however, increased the range of the EBITDA per metric ton guidance from the current INR 19,000 to INR 21,000 per metric ton to INR 24,000 to INR 25,000 per metric ton.

evidence.fact: The company expects Q1 volume delivery close to the higher end of the 6% to 8% range.
evidence.quote: Q1, we are looking that you'll be able to -- we'll be delivering close to the higher end of the volume guidance range of 6% to 8%.

evidence.fact: Q1 EBITDA per metric ton is expected at the higher end of the range of INR19,000 to INR21,000.
evidence.quote: And EBITDA as well at the higher end of the range of INR19,000 to INR21,000 metric tonne.

evidence.fact: Consolidated volumes grew by 5% year-on-year with mid-single-digit growth in both segments.
evidence.quote: Against this backdrop, I am pleased to report a meaningful recovery in growth momentum. Consolidated volumes grew by 5% year-on-year with both our segments growing in mid-single-digit.

evidence.fact: India region volumes grew by 11% driven by double-digit growth in performance segment and high single-digit growth in specialty products.
evidence.quote: India, our primary engine grew by an impressive 11% led by double-digit growth in performance segment and high single-digit growth in specialty products.

evidence.fact: Rest of the World region volume grew by 6% year-on-year, led by demand recovery in The Americas and strong performance at TRI-K.
evidence.quote: Rest of the World region volume grew by 6% year-on-year. The Americas led the growth as demand recovered following greater clarity on tariff-related developments, while our premium specialty business at TRI-K continued its strong performance.

evidence.fact: The EPC project in Mexico continues to progress as planned and remains on track for commercialization over the next 12 months.
evidence.quote: I'm also pleased with the progress being made with our EPC project in Mexico. The project continues to progress as planned, contributing EPC service income during the quarter, and we remain on track for commercialization over the next 12 months.

evidence.fact: The company incurs an annual capex of INR 150 crores to INR 200 crores.
evidence.quote: It's all part of that INR 150 crores to INR 200 crores capex that we incur every year because we also do preparing anticipation of certain businesses fructifying because if we don't have the capacity, we can't even start the market development exercise.

evidence.fact: Capital expenditure for the current year will be about an additional listing of about INR 150 crores.
evidence.quote: So I think this year, we will be at about an additional listing of about INR 150 crores.

evidence.fact: The company reported its highest ever quarterly EBITDA of INR 252.5 crores.
evidence.quote: Today, as we report our highest ever quarterly EBITDA of INR 252.5 crores, I believe we are beginning to see the benefits of the capabilities, enduring relationships and strategic foundations that we have been building over the last several years.

evidence.fact: EBITDA stood at INR 252.5 crores compared to INR 135.1 crores in Q1 FY26.
evidence.quote: For quarter one, I'm pleased to inform you all that the EBITDA stood at INR 252.5 crores compared to INR 135.1 crores in Q1 FY26, while EBITDA per metric ton improved to INR 35,458 per metric ton from approximately INR 20,009 per metric ton in the corresponding period last year.

evidence.fact: EBITDA grew 87% YoY to Rs 252 Cr and EBITDA per MT improved to Rs 35,458.
evidence.quote: Strong earnings recovery, with EBITDA growing 87% YoY to ₹252 Cr and EBITDA/MT improving to ₹35,458/MT, driven by disciplined pricing, a favourable product mix within the Specialty Care segment, operational excellence, improved operating leverage and robust risk management, despite a volatile raw material environment

evidence.fact: India volumes grew 8% year-on-year in Q4.
evidence.quote: India volumes grew 8% year-on-year, driven by a 3% growth in performance and more than 27% growth in specialty volumes.

evidence.fact: AMET volumes declined 15% year-on-year in Q4 due to logistics and raw material availability constraints.
evidence.quote: In contrast, the AMET region remains challenging for reasons outlined earlier with volumes declining 15% year-on-year in Q4.

evidence.fact: Rest of the world volumes declined 7% year-on-year in Q4 while delivering 4% growth on a full year basis.
evidence.quote: The rest of the world region witnessed mixed trends with volumes declining 7% year-on-year in Q4 while delivering a 4% growth on a full year basis.

evidence.fact: AMET operations faced disruptions during April and early May due to developments in West Asia.
evidence.quote: The development in the West Asia created significant disruptions across the region during April and early May, impacting both inbound and outbound supply chains. Our Egypt operations were also affected during this period.

evidence.fact: Longer transit times, port congestion and elevated freight costs continue to require close monitoring.
evidence.quote: Longer transit times, port congestion and elevated freight costs continue to be the areas that require close monitoring.

evidence.fact: Management remains watchful of evolving geopolitical developments and their impact on global supply chains.
evidence.quote: While we remain watchful of evolving geopolitical developments and their impact on global supply chains, we are encouraged by the recovery in customer demand, the strong momentum in Specialty Care and the continued strength of our India business.
